facts.text: Dugspur is an unincorporated community in Carroll County, Virginia, located along U.S. Route 221, about 8 miles east-northeast of Hillsville.
The community sits at an elevation of roughly 2,661 feet, giving it a cool, humid subtropical climate with mild winters and warm summers.
Dugspur’s name honors Charles Carroll of Carrollton, the last surviving signer of the Declaration of Independence, rather than John Carroll himself.
Early settlers were Scotch‑Irish immigrants who arrived after the Revolutionary War, drawn by high‑altitude land grants despite tough soils.
The area’s first inhabitants were Native Americans who lived there for about 10,000 years before European arrival.
Dugspur emerged as a distinct settlement in the late 18th century, closely tied to Quaker communities that promoted mutual aid and anti‑slavery sentiments.
